title: Pipeline simulator: a world to watch and play with
summary: Owner wish of 24 November 2026: simulate and show card throughput per phase and token usage, to understand bottlenecks, development and costs, in the spirit of an interactive simulation site (a world you watch move, then play with). Proposal: a project hub section Pipeline world next to Throughput & cycle time. A live isometric world fed by lane, step, token and quota events; a what-if fork from the current state with selectable strategies (strict, fast as built, fast as intended, dispatcher) and editable parameters; seven charts (cards per hour, queue per phase, bottleneck band, raw tokens and USD first pass and rework, lead time, weekly window); following one card; comparing two runs. A per-card discrete-event engine in the backend calls the decision library's policies, so simulated rules are the shipped ones; dated parameter sets are measured nightly and checked by replaying 17, 18 and 23 November. No model tokens. A first wave model of the 57-card wave puts the bottleneck at integration under strict (3.3 cards/h, median gate wait 167 min) and at coding under fast as intended (6.6 cards/h); about one weekly point per card; it misses the measured 40 % rework share (12.5 %). Twelve decisions, nine slices in a backend and a frontend lane.

openDecisions.title: Where the engine runs
openDecisions.question: Where does the simulation engine run, and where do its rules come from?

options.A: In the browser, its own TypeScript rules
options.B: In the backend, a .NET engine that calls the decision library's policies; the browser plays back the event log
options.C: Both, a browser estimate plus the backend engine

openDecisions.recommendation: B. In the backend, a .NET engine that calls the decision library's policies; the browser plays back the event log
openDecisions.rationale: A simulated strategy must be the shipped strategy; rules live only in orchestration-decisions/.

openDecisions.title: Model granularity
openDecisions.question: How fine is the model?

options.B: Per-card discrete events, seeded, 200 runs for a range

openDecisions.recommendation: B. Per-card discrete events, seeded, 200 runs for a range
openDecisions.rationale: Loops compound per card; averages hide the 7-round card.

openDecisions.title: Where it lives
openDecisions.question: Where does the simulator appear in the Studio?

options.A: Project hub section Pipeline world next to Throughput & cycle time
options.B: A tab inside Throughput & cycle time
options.C: A workspace-level route for all projects

openDecisions.recommendation: A. Project hub section Pipeline world next to Throughput & cycle time
openDecisions.rationale: Gate, window, strategy and conflicts are per project; a full-bleed world needs its own section.

openDecisions.title: Source of the live mode
openDecisions.question: How is the live world fed?

options.B: Snapshot on open, then events over /hubs/jobs

openDecisions.recommendation: B. Snapshot on open, then events over /hubs/jobs
openDecisions.rationale: The events exist; a picture that lags 30 s cannot show a card moving.

openDecisions.title: Telling the modes apart
openDecisions.question: How are live and what-if told apart at a glance?

options.B: Ground, figure style, mode pill with change chips, and a forked timeline together

openDecisions.recommendation: B. Ground, figure style, mode pill with change chips, and a forked timeline together
openDecisions.rationale: A simulated queue must never be read as a real one, even in a screenshot.

openDecisions.title: Visual language
openDecisions.question: How much of the inspiration's look is taken?

options.A: Its palette and Archivo as a separate simulator theme
options.B: Its principle with Studio tokens, lane tones and Inter at weight 800 with system fallback
options.C: As B, plus a bundled Archivo for the headline only

openDecisions.recommendation: B. Its principle with Studio tokens, lane tones and Inter at weight 800 with system fallback
openDecisions.rationale: One visual system, both themes, no font from another host; C stays open if the headline looks weak.

openDecisions.title: Rendering of the world
openDecisions.question: What draws the world?

options.B: Canvas 2D for the world, inline SVG for charts

openDecisions.recommendation: B. Canvas 2D for the world, inline SVG for charts
openDecisions.rationale: Hundreds of moving figures; charts stay in the existing SVG pattern; no new dependency.

openDecisions.title: Parameter refresh
openDecisions.question: How are parameters refreshed?

options.B: Nightly dated set from a 7-day window, owner changes as a named layer, slots and quota read live at the fork

openDecisions.recommendation: B. Nightly dated set from a 7-day window, owner changes as a named layer, slots and quota read live at the fork
openDecisions.rationale: Reproducible comparisons need sets that never change once written.

openDecisions.title: When the model is trusted
openDecisions.question: What makes a parameter set usable for decisions?

options.B: Replay of 17, 18 and 23 November within 15 % throughput, 25 % median gate wait, 20 % USD; nightly fit shown

openDecisions.recommendation: B. Replay of 17, 18 and 23 November within 15 % throughput, 25 % median gate wait, 20 % USD; nightly fit shown
openDecisions.rationale: The first model misses the rework share by a factor of three; only a replay shows that.

openDecisions.title: Model tokens
openDecisions.question: May the simulator use model tokens?

options.A: No; statements and bottleneck readings are computed
options.B: A persona narration of a run on the persona budget

openDecisions.recommendation: A. No; statements and bottleneck readings are computed
openDecisions.rationale: The simulation is arithmetic over records; a narration can be added later as a persona action.

openDecisions.title: Judging dispatcher strategies
openDecisions.question: Where are dispatcher strategies replayed?

options.B: On this engine through DispatchPlanPolicy; DS-4 uses it

openDecisions.recommendation: B. On this engine through DispatchPlanPolicy; DS-4 uses it
openDecisions.rationale: Two simulators of the same pipeline would disagree; one engine serves both.

openDecisions.title: Use of the research prototypes
openDecisions.question: How do the two prototype variants feed in?

options.B: Take findings from both into SIM-3, SIM-6 and SIM-8; engine from SIM-2

openDecisions.recommendation: B. Take findings from both into SIM-3, SIM-6 and SIM-8; engine from SIM-2
openDecisions.rationale: Prototype rules would be a copy outside the decision library; their visual findings are the value.

# SIM-1 · Recorded facts and the simulation event schema

Source: `docs/pipeline-simulator/index.html` (AGT-4028) and its pages `model.html`, `world.html`, `surfaces.html`, plus `workbench.json`. Dependencies: none.

**Area:** backend/Features/Simulation/Facts (new), contracts, docs

## Why
Dossier pages Model (Entities, Parameters) and The world (Two modes). The live world and the engine both need one event vocabulary and one snapshot of the current state. The facts exist in separate places: IntegrationLaneEvent (backend/Features/Pipeline/IntegrationLaneEvents.cs), PipelineStepExecution in pipeline-execution.json, task.json token receipts through ProjectTokenLedger, quota history, the batch gate ledger and the conflict record.

## Deliver
1. A versioned simulation event schema: time, project, card key, kind, phase, slot, round number, run kind (first pass, sync round, fix round, repair, review), model and level, the four token counters and list-price USD (through TokenPricingService), plus a run id (null when recorded), stable receipt id and receipt timestamp for de-duplication and token bucketing. Normalize the four counters into disjoint categories; keep missing counters unknown rather than zero. Lane event kinds map onto it one to one.
2. `GET /api/projects/{p}/simulation/snapshot`: every non-terminal card with phase, slot or queue position, elapsed time in phase, round number, base commit; slot counts and occupancy; gate and window state; quota used percent and reset per provider.
3. `GET /api/projects/{p}/simulation/days/{yyyy-MM-dd}`: the recorded event log of a UTC day, rebuilt from the sources above, with a list of gaps (facts that could not be found) instead of zeros.
4. Add the round number to review rows of the token analysis fold so reviews split into first pass and rework without a new usage kind; totals unchanged.
5. A pure projection test over fixed fixtures; a domain page section in docs/system/domains/pipeline.md (or a new docs/system/domains/simulation.md) and one row for docs/pipeline-simulator/index.html in docs/start/README.md.

## Acceptance
- The snapshot of a fixture workspace lists every in-flight card once, and its counts per phase equal the board's.
- A recorded fixture day replays into the schema with no unexplained gap; first pass plus rework USD equals the token analysis total for that day.
- No model call, no write path; the endpoints are read-only.

# SIM-2 · Simulation engine on the decision library

Source: `docs/pipeline-simulator/index.html` (AGT-4028) and its pages `model.html`, `world.html`, `surfaces.html`, plus `workbench.json`. Dependencies: SIM-1.

**Area:** backend/Features/Simulation/Engine (new), orchestration-decisions/ (moved pure rules)

## Why
Dossier pages Model (Phases, Loops, Strategies) and decision PS-D1 B, PS-D2 B. The engine must apply the shipped rules: BatchFormationPolicy, BatchGateStartPolicy, BisectVerdictPolicy and RedTestTriagePolicy in orchestration-decisions/. The window close rule (runner/PostMergeRunPlan.cs) and the stale-verdict check of the review plane are pure but live outside the library.

## Deliver
1. Move the window close rule and the stale-verdict threshold check into orchestration-decisions/ as pure policies with their existing tests; callers use them unchanged. No other rule changes.
2. A deterministic, seeded discrete-event engine: entities card, run, slot pool, queue, develop, batch, window, quota window; phases Ready, Coding, Review, Integration, Done; loops conflict, red gate, stale verdict, red after integration. It starts from a SIM-1 snapshot or from an empty project with an arrival wave, and emits SIM-1 events with a run id.
3. Strategy as three choices (test placement, gate shape, dispatch rule) with presets strict, fast as built, fast as intended, and a dispatch slot that defaults to today's order. A preset whose policy does not exist yet is flagged as a design model.
4. `POST /api/projects/{p}/simulation/runs` (parameters, strategy, seed or seed count, horizon) returning the event log and per-run summary; 200 seeds return percentiles. Runs are kept in memory with a bounded cache; nothing is written to job folders.
5. A port of docs/pipeline-simulator/evidence/wave_model.py's scenario as an engine test: with its parameters the engine reproduces its table within the seed range, or the report explains each difference by a shipped rule the Python model lacks.

## Acceptance
- Same seed, same input: identical event log. A 57-card wave with 200 seeds runs in under 5 s on the host.
- The engine contains no transition rule of its own; an architecture test fails when it does (extend TransitionDecisionBoundaryTests or add a Simulation boundary test).
- No model call.
